title: bug: the delivery policy re-derives a DONE task's required check from current settings and epic shape, so a later edit withholds its dependents
description:
Found by the Wave 1 integration gate (task-808869c5, adversarial pass) and confirmed with a scratch vitest probe against evaluateDeliveryEvidence.

requiredCheckCommand(state, task) reads settings.autoCommit, qualityGate, qualityGateScope and isEpicFinalTask when the evidence is JUDGED. For a DONE task that required check is re-judged every time: the status rule acceptance criterion 2 forces. So the requirement is whatever the project says now, not what was due when the task landed.
1. Archiving, deleting or reordering an epic's final task makes an earlier DONE task epic-final. Under the default epicFinal scope, that task landed with its gate deferred: no candidate and no check. It now "requires" a check that nothing short of a new landing can produce, and every task naming it in dependsOn or blockedOnTaskIds becomes unclaimable (DEPENDENCY_EVIDENCE_MISSING).
   Probe: before the archive {satisfied:true}; after {satisfied:false, missingEvidence:['required-check:node gate.cjs']}.
2. Changing settings.qualityGate re-judges every DONE task against the NEW command.
   Probe: a DONE task with a runner-observed exit-0 run of 'node gate.cjs' on its current candidate reports ['required-check:node other-gate.cjs'] missing once the setting changes.
3. The same happens when qualityGateScope switches to everyTask, or when a project with history turns on a strict deliveryPolicy.

No project here runs a strict policy today (this repository is legacy), so the impact is latent. It lands on the first adopter, and there is no operator escape short of set_task_dependencies.
definitionOfDone: A recorded design decision: bind the required check to what was due at delivery (for example the required command, or none, recorded on the candidate or receipt or at the DONE transition), or keep re-judging with an explicit operator escape. Held-out acceptance criterion 2 stays green with no assertion edited
The two probes (archive of the epic-final sibling; a qualityGate change after DONE) are regression tests that fail on today's code and pass after the fix
docs/CONFIGURATION.md's deliveryPolicy row states which settings are read at delivery time and which at judge time

implementationPlan.description:
TDD + schema. Add the optional snapshot field and tests that fail on today's re-derive.

In packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts, on Task, next to deliveryEvidence:
```
/**
 * Gate command that was due at the DONE transition (qa_approve), or null if none was.
 * Absent (undefined) means not snapshotted: a record written before this field, or a DONE that skipped qa_approve. Additive; no schemaVersion bump.
 */
requiredCheckAtDone?: string | null;
```

In packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts, inside `describe('delivery policy — evaluateDeliveryEvidence')`, add three tests. Do not edit acceptance.test.ts. Reuse seedPrerequisite / STRICT_SETTINGS / GATE / RUNNER_PASS.

1) Archive probe (must FAIL on current policy.ts):
- seedPrerequisite({ settings: { ...STRICT_SETTINGS, qualityGateScope: 'epicFinal' }, task: { requiredCheckAtDone: null, order: 1 }, siblings: [{ id: 'task-final', status: 'DONE', order: 2 }], checks: [] })

- await h.state.updateTask('task-final', { status: 'ARCHIVED' })

2) qualityGate-change probe (must FAIL on current policy.ts):

- await h.state.updateSettings({ qualityGate: 'node other-gate.cjs' })
- after: still satisfied:true with missingEvidence [] (today's code reports ['required-check:node other-gate.cjs']).

3) qa_approve persists the live command (or null) onto requiredCheckAtDone at DONE. Use the existing seed()/qa_approve helpers in this file: a mid-epic REVIEW task under epicFinal scope must write requiredCheckAtDone: null; an epic-final (or everyTask) task with a passing runner-observed check must write the trimmed qualityGate string. Assert the on-disk task JSON as well as state.getTask.

In packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.test.ts, extend the existing `UPDATE_TASK strips the delivery-evidence label` case (or a sibling it) so a payload `requiredCheckAtDone: null` (or a forged command) does not clobber a stored snapshot. implementationPlan.description:
Minimum impl so step 1's tests pass. Root-cause fix is one read site (evaluateDeliveryEvidence), not a guard at each caller.

In packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/policy.ts:
- Keep requiredCheckCommand as the LIVE derivation (autoCommit === false → null; blank qualityGate → null; qualityGateScope !== 'everyTask' && !isEpicFinalTask → null; else trimmed gate). Callers that need 'what the wrapper would run NOW' stay on it.
- In evaluateDeliveryEvidence, after the legacy short-circuit and landing split, resolve the check command as: if LANDING_JUDGED.has(task.status) && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(task, 'requiredCheckAtDone'), use the snapshot; else requiredCheckCommand(state, task).
- Snapshot rules: null or whitespace-only string → no check due. A non-empty string → trim and use as today (hasPassingCheck already trims the recorded run). Error handling: a snapshot that is neither string nor null is unreadable — logger.warn, treat as a required check that is missing (do not throw; the only throw remains an unrecognised deliveryPolicy). Lookup failures in hasPassingCheck stay as they are (log, missing).
- Update the file-header comment: landing evidence is judged at the DONE transition; the required check is judged live until DONE, then bound to requiredCheckAtDone.

In packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/qaApprove.ts, on the updateTask that flips to DONE (~204), always set requiredCheckAtDone: requiredCheckCommand(state, task) — including under legacy, including null. Compute it after the evidence gate so a refused approval writes nothing. Do not try/catch around the write; existing tool error handling applies.

In packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts UPDATE_TASK_DENYLIST, add 'requiredCheckAtDone' next to 'deliveryEvidence' with a one-line comment that a board client must not forge or wipe the snapshot.

Do not edit wrappers, acceptance.test.ts, SCHEMA.md, or Kotlin. Do not bump schemaVersion. Do not clear the field in buildReopenClearingUpdates (inert while status is not DONE/ARCHIVED; the next qa_approve overwrites).

Re-run `npx vitest run src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts src/server/WebSocketServer.test.ts`; expect PASS. Confirm src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts was not touched.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN: `npx vitest run src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts src/server/WebSocketServer.test.ts` -> 160 passed (was 11 failed | 149 passed before impl); `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0. acceptance.test.ts untouched (not in git diff).
Impl: policy.ts new checkShortfall(state, task) = the one read site; evaluateDeliveryEvidence uses it. DONE/ARCHIVED + snapshot: null/blank -> none owed, string -> trimmed command, other type -> logger.warn + new token 'unreadable-required-check' (EVIDENCE_TOKENS.unreadableRequiredCheck, with a TOKEN_REASONS entry so claim_next_task's describeMissingEvidence explains it; never throws). qaApprove.ts writes requiredCheckAtDone: requiredCheckCommand(state, task) in the DONE updateTask payload (after every gate; under every policy incl. legacy). WebSocketServer.ts denylists requiredCheckAtDone.
Two deliberate deviations from the plan text, both mutation-proven:
(1) Discriminator is `snapshot === undefined`, not hasOwnProperty. An update carrying requiredCheckAtDone: undefined leaves an own key holding undefined in memory (taskStore spreads updates), which hasOwnProperty misreads as a malformed snapshot. Mutation M2 (hasOwnProperty) turns the reopen test red with ['unreadable-required-check']. null vs omitted is still distinguished (strict ===), so the plan's `!= null` warning still holds.
(2) buildReopenClearingUpdates now clears requiredCheckAtDone (plan said not to). Reason: set_task_status/board allow DONE->WORKING->REVIEW->DONE without qa_approve, and a stale null snapshot would then release dependents with no check even when one is now owed: a fail-open regression vs today's live rule. Mutation M1 (line removed) turns 'drops the snapshot on reopen...' red ([] instead of ['required-check:node gate.cjs']). Scope grew by util/reopen.ts (+3 lines). Mutation M3 (status guard removed) turns 'ignores a snapshot on a task that is not DONE or ARCHIVED' red. All mutants restored, sha1 verified.
Added tests this step: snapshot reads (whitespace -> none, number/object -> unreadable token), not-DONE ignores snapshot, reopen drops snapshot (real set_task_status path).

implementationPlan.description:
Document delivery-time vs judge-time in docs/CONFIGURATION.md's `deliveryPolicy` table row (the long cell, not a new setting). State explicitly:
- Judge time (every evaluateDeliveryEvidence call): settings.deliveryPolicy itself — `legacy` still short-circuits to satisfied; a strict value still requires the landing tokens for not-yet-DONE tasks.
- Delivery time (qa_approve, persisted as task.requiredCheckAtDone): autoCommit, qualityGate (trimmed), qualityGateScope, and whether the task was epic-final among non-ARCHIVED siblings. A later archive/reorder/qualityGate/autoCommit edit must not change a DONE/ARCHIVED task's required check.
- Absent requiredCheckAtDone (legacy rows, fixtures, DONE via set_task_status/board move): fall back to live requiredCheckCommand. That is the remaining re-judge path and the reason held-out criterion 2 needs no assertion edit.
- The wrapper still decides whether to RUN the gate from live settings; the daemon only records what was due at approval.
Do not rewrite the rest of the row. Skill: ponytail — this file only.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Three options: (1) keep re-judging requiredCheckCommand from live settings/epic shape and add an operator escape (set_task_dependencies / a new MCP override); (2) snapshot the required command on the Candidate or DeliveryReceipt at wrapper record time; (3) snapshot at the DONE transition on the task and use that snapshot when status is DONE/ARCHIVED. (1) is rejected: the DoD allows it but it leaves the latent first-adopter bug and makes every archive/qualityGate edit a human unstick. (2) is rejected: both records are wrapper-called and IMMUTABLE, criterion 2's fixtures have neither field, and adding inputs to record_candidate/record_delivery_receipt is a launcher change the epic rail forbids. (3) is the decision: daemon-only, written by qa_approve, read only for LANDING_JUDGED statuses. Absent field falls back to live requiredCheckCommand so held-out acceptance criterion 2 (everyTask + no snapshot on the DONE fixture) stays green with no assertion edited. Always snapshot, including under legacy, so a later switch to a strict deliveryPolicy does not re-derive a check that was not due at approval. Rejected: treating a missing snapshot as 'none due' — that would make criterion 2's failed-gate DONE prerequisite look satisfied.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: evaluateDeliveryEvidence in packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/policy.ts already splits landing evidence (skipped when status is DONE/ARCHIVED via LANDING_JUDGED) from the required check (always live requiredCheckCommand). requiredCheckCommand reads state.project.settings.autoCommit, qualityGate (trimmed), qualityGateScope, and isEpicFinalTask (non-ARCHIVED siblings, same as get_context). hasPassingCheck binds to the current candidate's tree, trimmed command, exit 0, runner-observed; lookup failures log and report missing (fail closed). qa_approve.ts ~128 evaluates evidence then updateTask to DONE; that is the one write that must persist the snapshot. Plugin UPDATE_TASK is denylisted in WebSocketServer.ts UPDATE_TASK_DENYLIST (deliveryEvidence is already there) — the new field must join it or a board client can forge requiredCheckAtDone:null and unstick dependents. Task JSON load is loadEntities (raw JSON.parse), so createTask({ requiredCheckAtDone: null }) round-trips. Tests for evaluateDeliveryEvidence already live in src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts (seedPrerequisite); put the two probes there. Do NOT edit src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts. h.state.updateSettings exists for the qualityGate-change probe; updateTask({ status: 'ARCHIVED' }) for the archive probe. Kotlin Task data class has no requiredCheckAtDone — Gson drops unknown keys on the wire; the field stays on disk. Do not add JetBrains UI in this task.
planningNotes.risks: Criterion 2's DONE fixture has no snapshot: fallback to live is mandatory or the held-out test goes red. JSON null vs omitted is the snapshot/legacy discriminator — use Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(task, 'requiredCheckAtDone'), not != null. A malformed snapshot (not string and not null) must fail closed (report the check missing, log warn) and must not throw (evaluateDeliveryEvidence throws only for an unrecognised deliveryPolicy). qa_approve under legacy must still write the snapshot. set_task_status / board-move to DONE still skips the snapshot (existing 'judged outside qa_approve' hole); document it. Do not bump schemaVersion. Do not change wrappers. Error handling for plugin forgery is the denylist, not a sanitize-and-accept. Shared checkout: qaApprove.test.ts may be dirty from peers — only edit the new cases.

completionSummary:
Decision: bind the required check to what was due at delivery. qa_approve writes task.requiredCheckAtDone = requiredCheckCommand(state, task) (trimmed gate, or null) on the DONE update under every policy, legacy included. delivery/policy.ts checkShortfall() is the single read site: a DONE/ARCHIVED task with a snapshot owes that check (null/blank = none; any other type -> logger.warn + new token 'unreadable-required-check', never throws, never satisfied); a task not yet DONE, or one without a snapshot, uses the live rule, so held-out criterion 2 stays green unedited. WebSocketServer UPDATE_TASK_DENYLIST gains requiredCheckAtDone. docs/CONFIGURATION.md deliveryPolicy row states judge-time vs delivery-time settings.
Two plan deviations, both mutation-proven: (1) absent is detected with `=== undefined`, not hasOwnProperty, because taskStore.updateTask spreads updates, so a `field: undefined` write leaves an own key holding undefined in memory; (2) util/reopen.ts buildReopenClearingUpdates now clears the snapshot. Without that, DONE -> reopen -> DONE via set_task_status or the board would reuse a stale null and release dependents with no check (fail-open vs today).
Tests: the archive probe and the qualityGate-change probe (both red on old code with the issue's exact tokens), the qa_approve snapshot on disk and in memory (trimmed gate, null mid-epic, null autoCommit=false, legacy writes), malformed/blank snapshot reads, not-DONE ignores snapshot, reopen drops snapshot (real set_task_status path), and the WS forgery case. Red: 11 failed before the fix. Regression: 40 related files, 1175/1175 pass. tsc clean.
